name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)
pathway_notes: One of the world's top STEM universities. Extremely competitive admissions with a 4% acceptance rate. Research opportunities are exceptional — undergraduates routinely publish papers. Strong entrepreneurship ecosystem and startup culture through MIT Sandbox and The Engine.
affordability_notes: Need-blind admissions for US students. Meets 100% of demonstrated financial need. Families earning under $90K pay nothing. Average aid package is substantial.

name: Stanford University
pathway_notes: Premier university with unmatched connections to Silicon Valley tech and venture capital. 4% acceptance rate. Offers unusual flexibility through its major-declaration timeline. Proximity to Google, Apple, Meta headquarters creates exceptional internship pipelines.
affordability_notes: Need-blind, meets 100% of demonstrated need. Families earning under $100K pay nothing. Average net price for families earning under $150K has been under $20K.

name: Carnegie Mellon University
pathway_notes: Globally recognized for computer science, robotics, and the arts. School of Computer Science and School of Drama are both top-ranked — rare combination. Game design program is among the best in the world. Strong industry placement in tech, finance, and entertainment.
affordability_notes: Need-blind admissions. Merit scholarships available through individual programs. Aid packages are competitive but families may expect significant contributions at higher income levels.

name: UC Berkeley
pathway_notes: Top public university in the world. 11% acceptance rate for in-state, lower for out-of-state. Extremely strong in STEM, social sciences, and environmental fields. Berkeley sits at the edge of the Bay Area tech ecosystem with deep ties to startups and labs.
affordability_notes: Significantly more affordable for California residents ($14K/year tuition). Cal Grant covers full tuition for eligible California students with household incomes under $110K. Out-of-state costs are much higher.

name: Georgia Institute of Technology
pathway_notes: One of the best values in engineering education nationally. Strong co-op program — students alternate semesters of study with paid industry work, graduating with 1-2 years of experience. Atlanta location provides access to Delta, Coca-Cola, CNN, and numerous tech companies.
affordability_notes: Outstanding value for Georgia residents (~$12K/year tuition). Zell Miller Scholarship covers full tuition for eligible Georgia students. Out-of-state tuition is roughly $30K but competitive with peer institutions.

name: Northeastern University
pathway_notes: Famous for its cooperative education (co-op) program — students alternate classroom semesters with 6-month full-time paid work experiences. By graduation, students have up to 18 months of professional experience. Employers routinely hire co-op students into full-time roles. Boston location provides access to biotech, finance, and tech sectors.
affordability_notes: Tuition is high (~$60K/year), but co-op earnings can offset $20K-$40K over the degree. Merit scholarships are widely available. Aid packages vary significantly by family income.

name: Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT)
pathway_notes: Strong applied focus with excellent co-op program. Top-ranked game design and animation programs. One of the most accessible universities for deaf and hard-of-hearing students (NTID is located on campus). Cybersecurity program is nationally recognized.
affordability_notes: Tuition around $55K/year. Merit scholarships are widely available and competitive. Co-op earnings offset cost significantly. Aid is available based on need.

name: Purdue University
pathway_notes: Outstanding engineering and agriculture programs at public university prices. 23 Purdue alumni have flown in space — the most of any university. Strong placement in aerospace, defense, and manufacturing. Purdue's online division is a major pathway for working students.
affordability_notes: Frozen in-state tuition for many recent years (around $10K-$12K). Out-of-state tuition is around $28K. Significant merit and need-based aid available.

name: Penn State University
pathway_notes: One of the largest alumni networks in the world (700,000+ members) — a significant career asset. Campuses across Pennsylvania make it accessible statewide. Strong programs in business, engineering, communications, and agriculture.
affordability_notes: In-state tuition around $18K-$20K. Out-of-state costs are significantly higher. Financial aid and merit scholarships are available. 24 campuses offer lower-cost entry options.

name: Arizona State University
pathway_notes: The most innovative university in the US for 9 consecutive years (US News). Broad access mission — no student turned away for academic reasons. Exceptional online programs allow students to earn an ASU degree anywhere in the world. Strong programs in sustainability, journalism, and film. Tempe campus is large with an active social and research culture.
affordability_notes: Affordable for Arizona residents (around $12K/year). Online programs are among the most affordable in the country ($10K/year total for many degrees). Merit-based New American University Scholarship is automatic for eligible students.

name: Western Governors University (WGU)
pathway_notes: Competency-based online university — you advance by demonstrating mastery, not seat time. Full-time students can often complete degrees in 2-3 years. Strong for working adults and career changers. Industry certifications (AWS, CompTIA, CISCO) are embedded in technology programs. Regionally and nationally accredited.
affordability_notes: Flat-rate tuition of approximately $3,500-$4,200 per 6-month term regardless of credits completed. No traditional financial aid requirement issues — very affordable. Scholarships available.

name: Rhode Island School of Design (RISD)
pathway_notes: One of the most prestigious art and design schools in the world. Rigorous studio-based education emphasizing craft, concept, and professional practice. Adjacent to Brown University with cross-registration opportunities. RISD graduates lead major design studios, tech companies (Google, Apple), and fashion houses. The portfolio is king in RISD admissions — GPA matters less than creative work.
affordability_notes: Tuition around $56K/year. Need-based aid is available. Portfolio quality is the most important admissions factor; strong aid packages go to high-need, talented students.

name: Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD)
pathway_notes: Large, professional art school with industry-level facilities. Strong industry partnerships — studios like Disney, Pixar, and Netflix recruit directly from SCAD. Programs in animation and game design are particularly strong. Multiple campus options including Atlanta, Lacoste (France), and online. Career services are unusually robust for an art school.
affordability_notes: Tuition around $38K/year. Merit scholarships widely available. Some international students receive significant scholarships. Financial aid available based on need.

name: Parsons School of Design (The New School)
pathway_notes: Located in New York City — the center of the American fashion and design industry. Direct access to internships at major fashion houses, media companies, and design firms. Part of The New School system, offering cross-registration with social sciences and liberal arts. Known for producing influential fashion designers. Industry portfolio reviews are built into curricula.
affordability_notes: Tuition around $55K/year. NYC cost of living adds significantly. Financial aid and scholarships are available but competitive.

name: Berklee College of Music
pathway_notes: The world's leading independent college of contemporary music. Alumni include Grammy-winning producers, film composers, and major label artists. Music production program is among the best in the world. Strong film scoring program. Music Business degree prepares students for industry roles in management, publishing, and marketing. Audition required; musical ability is the primary admissions factor.
affordability_notes: Tuition around $47K/year. Audition-based merit scholarships available. Many students receive awards based on musical talent. Online campus (Berklee Online) offers more affordable pathways.

name: The Juilliard School
pathway_notes: The most prestigious performing arts conservatory in the United States. Acceptance rate of around 8% — audition is everything. Classical performance preparation at the highest level. Graduates include some of the world's most celebrated musicians, actors, and dancers. Located at Lincoln Center in Manhattan. This is the path for students committed to elite performance careers.
affordability_notes: Tuition around $50K/year. Need-blind admissions for US students. Meets 100% of demonstrated financial need. Many students receive substantial aid. Talent is the deciding factor, not ability to pay.

name: Culinary Institute of America (CIA)
pathway_notes: America's most prestigious culinary college. Graduates run Michelin-starred restaurants, lead major food companies, and appear on television. Strong food business programs for students interested in entrepreneurship. Externship program places students in top kitchens nationwide. Faculty are working professionals — real-world connections are built-in.
affordability_notes: Tuition varies by program ($15K-$40K/year). Associate degrees are less expensive than bachelor's. Financial aid and culinary scholarships are available. Strong salary potential offsets costs for committed culinary professionals.

name: Johnson & Wales University
pathway_notes: Career-focused university with strong culinary, hospitality, and business programs. More accessible than CIA while still well-regarded in the industry. Internship and co-op programs are built into all degrees. Business programs (sports management, entrepreneurship) make it unique among culinary schools.
affordability_notes: Tuition around $35K/year. Merit scholarships are widely available. Financial aid based on need. More affordable than many private culinary programs.

name: United States Military Academy (West Point)
pathway_notes: Free full scholarship in exchange for 5 years of active military service after graduation. One of the most competitive and selective pathways in the United States — requires a congressional nomination. Produces Army officers who become leaders in business, government, and military. Outstanding academic programs alongside rigorous leadership training. West Point graduates lead Fortune 500 companies and government agencies.
affordability_notes: Completely free — tuition, room, board, and medical care are fully funded. Cadets receive a monthly stipend (~$1,100). In exchange, graduates serve 5 years on active duty as commissioned Army officers.

name: United States Naval Academy (USNA)
pathway_notes: Free full scholarship in exchange for 5 years of active military service as a Navy or Marine Corps officer. Requires congressional nomination. Rigorous academic program combined with physical training, leadership development, and naval science. Graduates go on to careers in naval warfare, aviation, submarines, and surface warfare — then into elite civilian careers.
affordability_notes: Completely free — tuition, room, board, and medical care fully funded. Midshipmen receive a monthly stipend. Graduates serve 5 years as commissioned officers in the Navy or Marine Corps.

name: Howard University
pathway_notes: America's most prestigious HBCU and a top producer of African American professionals. Located in Washington D.C. — direct access to federal agencies, nonprofits, law firms, and media organizations. Howard's alumni network is extraordinarily loyal and powerful. Strong pre-med, business, and communications programs. Capstone Scholars Program provides full scholarships to top students.
affordability_notes: Tuition around $30K/year. Full-ride Capstone Scholars Program for top admitted students. Strong institutional aid. Many students receive significant scholarships. Median student debt at graduation is lower than many comparable institutions.

name: Spelman College
pathway_notes: The nation's leading HBCU for Black women. Exceptional outcomes in STEM — Spelman produces more Black women who earn STEM PhDs than almost any other college in the US. Strong culture of academic excellence and leadership. Located in Atlanta's University Center alongside Morehouse, Clark Atlanta, and others — creating a vibrant Black academic community.
affordability_notes: Tuition around $25K/year. Scholarships widely available. Part of the Atlanta University Center financial aid consortium. Strong outcomes relative to cost.

name: Lincoln Tech
pathway_notes: Nationally recognized trade school system with campuses in major US cities. Programs run 12-24 months and lead directly to career-ready skills and industry certifications. Employer partnerships are strong — many graduates receive job offers before completing their programs. For students who want hands-on training without a 4-year degree, Lincoln Tech offers a clear path to well-paying careers.
affordability_notes: Program costs vary by location and field ($15K-$40K total). Financial aid (Pell Grants, student loans) available. Costs are much lower than a 4-year degree for similar earning potential in the trades.

name: Community College (Transfer Pathway)
pathway_notes: Community colleges are the most underrated pathway in American higher education. Students can complete the first two years of a bachelor's degree at a fraction of the cost, then transfer to a 4-year university — often with guaranteed admission (through programs like TAG in California or CAA in Virginia). Two-year terminal degrees (ADN nursing, welding, HVAC) lead directly to high-paying careers. The best strategy: take general education courses and transfer to your target 4-year school.
affordability_notes: Tuition ranges from $3,000-$10,000/year — the most affordable college option available. Pell Grants often cover full costs for low-income students. Transfer agreements with state universities allow students to save $40,000-$80,000 over a degree.

name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
pathway_notes: One of the original Public Ivy institutions. Exceptional value for North Carolina residents. Top-ranked journalism school. Outstanding public health program and medical school pipeline. Research Triangle (Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill) provides access to pharmaceutical, biotech, and tech employers. Strong community culture and one of the most beautiful campuses in the US.
affordability_notes: Outstanding value for NC residents (around $9,000/year tuition). Carolina Covenant provides full scholarships (no loans) for qualifying low-income NC students. Out-of-state costs are significantly higher (~$37K).

name: Florida A&M University (FAMU)
pathway_notes: Florida's only public HBCU and a Carnegie Research University. College of Pharmacy is one of the top producers of Black pharmacists in the nation. Business, engineering, and journalism programs are strong. Tallahassee location provides access to state government and Florida's growing tech and healthcare sectors. Spirited campus culture and strong alumni network.
affordability_notes: Excellent value for Florida residents (around $5,700/year tuition). Substantial institutional and federal aid available. Scholarships for high-achieving students. Strong ROI relative to peer HBCUs.

name: Colorado School of Mines
pathway_notes: Highly specialized public STEM university with exceptional job placement rates and salaries — engineering graduates average among the highest starting salaries of any public university. Located near Denver, with access to energy, aerospace, and defense employers. Small, focused campus culture where STEM is the primary identity. Outdoor recreation access is exceptional given Colorado location.
affordability_notes: Competitive in-state tuition (~$19K/year). Financial aid available. High starting salaries after graduation make ROI excellent — median early-career salary for graduates is among the highest of any public university.
